fy_label_note: May fiscal year; Baba/VA FY labels equal company fiscal years (FY2022 = June 2021 to May 2022). VA operating margin runs about 30 to 50 bps below company adjusted EBIT (stage 3: FY2026 VA 12.84% at that pull vs adjusted EBIT 13.3%). VA FY2026 still carries a Q4 estimate (12.65%), so the five actual years are FY2021 to FY2025: 12.95%, 10.35%, 11.73%, 12.83%, 12.95%. Peers have December years, so each RPM year is compared with a calendar-weighted peer margin (7/12 of peer FY N-1 plus 5/12 of peer FY N). Sensitivity: peer FY2020 to FY2021 gives a 95 bps median decline (ratio 0.36); peer FY2021 to FY2022 gives 107 bps (0.41); the two-year peer window FY2020 to FY2022 gives 201 bps (0.78).

company.ltm_note: Q4 FY2025 to Q3 FY2026, last four VA actual quarters (operating income $976.0M on revenue $7,713.6M, data_compute). Company-reported FY2026 adjusted EBIT margin 13.3% (stage 3, DEF 14A doc 159267).
company.note: By FY2025, RPM's margin was back to its FY2021 level. Measured in VA operating margin, the 16% target is a level RPM has not reached at any point since at least FY2018 (peak 12.95%), so it is not the reversal of a cyclical compression.

peers.selection_note: Coatings (Sherwin-Williams, PPG, Akzo Nobel, Axalta from data_comps Paint & Coating) plus construction chemicals and adhesives (Sika, H.B. Fuller), which overlap RPM's Construction Products and Performance Coatings groups. Asian paint makers were dropped because their end markets differ.
peers.median_note: Calendar-weighted medians (middle two: PPG and AXTA in both periods). After the shock, the peer median recovered to about 15.5% in calendar 2024 (middle two SIK 14.71 and PPG 16.29, script-derived), above its pre-shock level, while RPM only returned to 12.95%.

relative_position_bps.post_recovery_note: About -255 bps in FY2025 vs the peer calendar 2024 median (script-derived), so the relative loss from the shock was never recovered.

track_record.note: No restatement or weakness surfaced in this pass (not specifically searched). Sullivan says margin improvement 'will require a return to unit volume growth in our Consumer business' (doc 68799, stage 3), which is a volume dependency, not a share-loss admission.

tenure.succession_note: David Dennsteadt named President and COO on 2026-07-17 (internal), which reads as CEO succession grooming.

deciding_facts: Pattern of missed targets under the same CEO: 16% EBIT was set in 2018, re-set for fiscal 2025 under MAP 2025 and missed again (FY2025 VA 12.95%, FY2026 adjusted 13.3%, 2024-2026 PSUs at 0%). The board's own new PSU target is 14% by May 2028.

The 2022 shock was real but only about 40% industry (ratio 0.40: peer median -105 bps vs RPM -260 bps, on RPM revenue +9.8%). RPM's gap to peers widened from -111 to -266 bps and has stayed around -255 bps since, because peers recovered above their pre-shock margins while RPM only returned to its FY2021 level.
confidence_note: The verdict holds under every peer alignment tested. Even the most macro-friendly alignment (ratio 0.78) leaves the missed-target pattern and the lasting relative gap. The fiscal-year alignment changes the ratio, not the call.
